messages:
maria (support): Heads up — ACME reporting p99 jump on /v1/generate starting ~03:10 PST. Customer shows tail spikes ~600ms on small prompts. They included a request id 0f3a7c. Raising for triage.

kevin (platform): Seen it on the org dashboard: <https://dashboards.redwood.local/d/latency/batcher-p95-p99?org=acme|batcher p95/p99 view>. Looks correlated with tiny prompt traffic bursts.

alice (sre-oncall): Can you paste an example payload and the request-id? Want to grep logs and check which pool.

maria (support): payload is like: {"prompt":"Hi","max_tokens":16}. Request id 0f3a7c (also 0f3a7d, 0f3a80 repeated). QPS ~420 over short bursts.

jon (eng-sre): That pattern screams coalesce/hold-time tradeoff. Tiny prompts + high QPS -> batcher holds for more requests to fill size -> few late arrivals cause high tail. What are current batcher params for that pool?

kevin (platform): Current config for the affected pool (prod-gpu-3):
```
batcher:
  grace_window_ms: 50
  max_batch_size: 64
  hold_timeout_ms: 200
  max_coalesce_delay_ms: 250
```

jon (eng-sre): Ok. hold_timeout 200ms is high for tiny prompts. Quick mitigation: reduce hold_timeout_ms and grace_window on that pool to prioritize latency. Recommend temporary: hold_timeout_ms: 20, grace_window_ms: 10. I'll roll a canary.

alice (sre-oncall): Deploying canary to pool prod-gpu-3-smallprompts (10% traffic) now. Command: `./opsctl rollout-batcher --pool prod-gpu-3 --config overrides/smallprompts.yml --pct 10`

batcher-bot: Canary deployed: prod-gpu-3-smallprompts @ 10% (canary_id=c-852). Monitoring metrics.

kevin (platform): After canary, short window: p99 dropped from ~920ms -> ~160ms for canary slice. Customer reported noticeable improvement. :thumbsup:

maria (support): ACME confirms improvements on their end, p95/p99 much better. They asked what changed.

jon (eng-sre): Quick note to explain: we lowered coalesce/hold to reduce waiting for batch fill. That increases per-token cost but fixed tail latency. We'll revert when we add adaptive batching for small prompts.

kevin (platform): Filed ticket INF-7261: "Adaptive coalesce for small payloads + routing policy" and linked this thread. Owner: @jon.

maria (support): Please add repro steps so support can run a local repro if customer sees regression.

jon (eng-sre): Repro steps (short):
1) Run loadgen with many tiny prompts (2-8 chars) in short bursts: 500 qps for 30s, then pause 10s, repeat.
2) Use the pool selector header to force prod-gpu-3.
3) Observe p99 on /v1/generate and check coalesce wait histogram.
Example loadgen command:
```bash
loadgen --url https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate \n  --concurrency 200 --qps 500 --duration 30s \n  --header 'X-Redwood-Pool: prod-gpu-3' \n  --body '{"prompt":"Hi","max_tokens":8}'
```

jon (eng-sre): Quick config we used for the canary (overrides/smallprompts.yml):
```
batcher:
  grace_window_ms: 10
  hold_timeout_ms: 20
  max_batch_size: 32
  small_prompt_threshold_tokens: 16
```

alice (sre-oncall): Rolling to 100% after positive canary. Rolling now.

batcher-bot: Rollout complete: prod-gpu-3-smallprompts @ 100% (canary_id=c-852). Keep an eye on cost delta.

kevin (platform): Longer-term mitigation items:
- implement adaptive hold based on recent prompt size distribution
- route tiny-prompt traffic to smaller batch-size pools automatically
- alert when small-prompt fraction > 30% for a pool
(see INF-7261)

maria (support): Thanks team — ACME is satisfied for now. I'll keep them updated and close the support ticket once we confirm 24h stability.

alice (sre-oncall): Monitoring dashboards pinned. We'll revert if any regression. Leaving this thread open for 24h.
